newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Ship delay to moor prices in high tide.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Ship delay to moor prices in high tide.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to remain firm due to prospects of a delay in shipping fresh supplies of the commodity from the Philippines, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Tuesday.

Talk that MV Blue Sapphire, which was supposed to load 35,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil for Rotterdam this month, was held up in China and not expected in Manila till next month pushed prices up last week, traders said.
"Expect a ride in rough waters this week as speculation on whether or not supplies from Indonesia can fill up market demand for nearby months continue to spread," said one trader.
Traders said coconut oil prices for nearby months increased by $5 per tonne last week after rumours of a delay on the loading schedule of MV Blue Sapphire hit the market.
There was talk in the market that another ship, MV Luctor, was contracted to pick up fresh coconut oil supplies for Rotterdam if Blue Sapphire fail to meet the schedule, traders said.
But Luctor was also scheduled to load this month fresh supplies for the U.S. market, they said.
Coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam dropped to 15,972 tonnes as of May 26 from the previous 19,475.
But traders said they expected coconut oil prices to drop in the long term due to improving supplies from both the Philippines and Indonesia.
The Philippine Coconut Authority said on Monday it expected exports of coconut products, including coconut oil, to increase between 1.6 and 1.8 million tonnes this year from last year's 1.5 million.
Despite prospects of rising harvests in the Philippines, the world's largest exporter of coconut products, big buyers of coconut oil have shifted to cheaper alternatives such as palm kernel oil.
Officials of Henkel KGaA of Germany and the U.S.-based Procter &Gamble Co have started using other vegetable oil for their products since the start of the year.
"Henkel and Procter retooled. They are now using substitutes on 30 percent of their (coconut oil) requirements," PCA administration Virgilio David said.
Traders said both firms require an estimated 200,000 tonnes of coconut oil yearly.
"I expect Henkel and Proter to shift back to the use of coconut oil," said a senior Manila trader, adding palm kernel oil is now trading at $15 to $20 premium over coconut oil.

"Coconut oil prices have gone down by more than $100 per tonne since the start of the year due to improving supplies from Manila and Jakarta because of improved weather conditions," the trader said. --Dolly Aglay (63 2) 841-8936, fax 817-6267
